metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to over-forecast (especially after spikes), apply downward correction lagged by 2–3 days.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast by 5–15% in next 3–5 days if sentiment turns neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust downward — apply mean reversion bias toward recent 7-day average if sentiment shifts.  
- Model overestimates volatility in sentiment-heavy periods — cap forecast range within ±10% of 14-day moving average if sentiment volatility > 0.7.  
- If true outcome is below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, model is overconfident — reduce forecast by 2–5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- When sentiment is positive but price declines, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — adjust forecast downward 1–3% per day if sentiment remains positive but price drops.
